title: Kloppy Integration
body:
I've been working on #160. Please find the draft in this PR.

It contains 2 files:
- `floodlight.io.from_kloppy`
- `from_kloppy.ipynb` to simply run everything and check it out.

I also have some questions:
- What is the purpose of "precedence" in the Teamsheet creation? Does it matter that we simply use the kloppy [PositionType](https://github.com/PySport/kloppy/blob/master/kloppy/domain/models/position.py#L4) enum to order here? This does do GK, DF, MF, FW, but the order within each line is for example LB, RB, LCB, RCB.
- Does floodlight enforce or rely on some specific orientation? I.e. home left, away right for the whole game?
- Does floodlight enforce or rely on a specific coordinate system with pitch dimensions? I'm currently transforming to "secondspectrum", because it seems your `Pitch` object needs a string name and "secondspectrum" is supported.
- I assume we rely on Period start and end frame ids? Are they really necessary, or only for creating XY objects?
- Does floodlight record different metadata for event and tracking data? (e.g. frame rate)
- Does floodlight not support z coordinates?
- I noticed In some xy_objects we have "HT1" "HT2" (e.g. second spectrum) and in others we get "firstHalf" and "secondHalf" (e.g. in IDSSEDataset). Does this matter?
- For events:
    - What is the purpose of `eID` and would it matter if we simply use [kloppy EventType](https://github.com/PySport/kloppy/blob/master/kloppy/domain/models/event.py#L285) for this?
    - Is `gameclock` seconds since start of period?
    - Is `outcome` 1.0 and 0.0? 
    - How much would it matter if `timestamp` is not a datetime, but a `timedelta` instead?
    - Is `qualifier` simply the raw event we get?

- [ ] Tests are still missing

title: Space-control aggregation returns numeric zero for fully unobserved frames
body:
## Summary When both teams have no observed player coordinates for a retained frame, `DiscreteVoronoiModel` preserves an all-`NaN` internal ownership grid, but its public aggregation methods return finite numeric values: - every player: `0.0` - Home: `0.0` - Away: `0.0` This converts: ```text no territorial-control observation exists ``` into: ```text an observed territorial-control value of zero ``` I would like maintainer guidance on treating this state as missing before preparing a production PR. The proposed initial repair is intentionally narrow: preserve temporal alignment and return `NaN` for player and team control only when the internal ownership frame contains no assigned owner. During reproduction, I also found broader observation-validity questions around one-team dropout, partial-player dropout, and motion-model derivative support. Those findings are documented below so that the narrow scope is an explicit design decision rather than an omission. --- ## Minimal reproduction ```python import numpy as np from floodlight import Pitch, XY from floodlight.models.space import DiscreteVoronoiModel pitch = Pitch.from_template("dfl", length=105, width=68, sport="football") missing_home = XY(np.full((3, 2), np.nan), framerate=10) missing_away = XY(np.full((3, 2), np.nan), framerate=10) model = DiscreteVoronoiModel( pitch, mesh="square", xpoints=10, motion_model="euclidean", ) model.fit(missing_home, missing_away) print(np.all(np.isnan(model._cell_controls_))) # True print(model.player_controls()[0].property) # currently [[0.], [0.], [0.]] print(model.team_controls()[0].property) # currently [[0.], [0.], [0.]] ``` The same public `0.0` behavior was reproduced for: - Euclidean ownership - Taki–Hasegawa ownership - Fujimura–Sugihara ownership - square meshes - hexagonal meshes --- ## Current mathematical behavior Let `G` be all mesh cells, `o_t(g)` the owner stored for cell `g` at frame `t`, `N_H` the number of Home players, and `i` a stacked player identifier. The current player aggregation is: ```text C_i(t) = round(100 * count(o_t(g) == i) / |G|, 2) ``` The current team aggregation is: ```text C_H(t) = round(100 * count(o_t(g) < N_H) / |G|, 2) C_A(t) = round(100 * count(o_t(g) >= N_H) / |G|, 2) ``` The denominator is always the total number of grid cells. For a completely unobserved frame, the producer retains an all-`NaN` ownership grid. Comparisons involving `NaN` are false, so every numerator is zero while the denominator remains nonzero: ```text 100 * 0 / |G| = 0 ``` The resulting `0.0` is therefore produced by aggregation mechanics rather than by an observed territorial partition. --- ## Shared architectural impact All supported configurations converge on the same internal ownership array and the same public aggregation boundary: ```text Home/Away XY inputs ↓ Euclidean, Taki–Hasegawa, or Fujimura–Sugihara costs ↓ square or hexagonal mesh ownership ↓ _cell_controls_ ↓ player_controls() team_controls() ``` The ownership producer already preserves the fully undefined state correctly as an all-`NaN` frame. Semantic information is lost only when `player_controls()` and `team_controls()` convert that frame into percentages. This means the defect affects every model/mesh path but has one shared, surgical repair boundary. --- ## Why this matters A finite zero normally communicates that a quantity was observed and measured as zero. That is not the state represented here: no ownership observation exists. The distinction matters for temporal averages, tactical summaries, frame-wise comparisons, downstream statistics, missing-data filtering, plotting, and reporting. The frame should remain present so temporal alignment is preserved. Its numerical output should communicate that the estimate is undefined. This is consistent with Floodlight's existing use of `NaN` in property, geometry, resampling, plotting, and aggregation workflows. --- ## Controlled reproduction and dropout-sensitivity experiment A deterministic synthetic experiment compared dropout-perturbed outputs with complete-data outputs from the same trajectories and model configuration. The experiment included: - 78 complete-data references - 2,220 deterministic dropout cases - 28,032 frame-level results - 0 failed cases - 0 nonfatal warnings - all three ownership models - both mesh types - representative mesh resolutions at `xpoints=10`, `20`, and `40` - six static formation families - three dynamic trajectory families - exact clean-process reproducibility These are implementation-specific synthetic sensitivity results. They do not establish real-world model accuracy, provider-wide dropout behavior, or a universal acceptable-error threshold.
Principal observation-validity findings ### Both teams fully unobserved Every tested path produced: ```text finite owner cells = 0 internal ownership = all NaN public player outputs = 0.0 public team outputs = 0.0 / 0.0 ``` This state is categorically non-estimable. ### One complete team unobserved Current output becomes a conserved `100/0` or `0/100` partition. Against matched complete-data references, maximum team-control error ranged from `36.25` to `63.46` percentage points. A numerically conserved 100% partition therefore does not establish that the observation is scientifically complete. ### Partial-player dropout When at least one player remains observed for each team, Floodlight partitions the pitch among the remaining players. The resulting estimand is territorial control conditional on the observed players. Across tested partial-dropout cases with both teams still represented: ```text maximum team error range: 0.00 to 60.38 percentage points leave-one-player-out maximum: 8.46 percentage points matched random-subset maximum: 22.19 percentage points ``` At identical 87.5% player coverage, different missing-player identities produced `0.00` versus `6.92` percentage-point team error. Player count or observed fraction is descriptive but cannot determine error by itself. ### Owned-cell coverage Whenever any valid player remained, the current producer assigned every grid cell, so `owned_cell_fraction = 1.0`. Only a completely unobserved frame produced `owned_cell_fraction = 0.0`. Owned-cell fraction therefore measures whether the algorithm produced any partition, not whether the tracking observation was complete. ### Motion-model temporal support Euclidean ownership remained frame-local. Taki–Hasegawa and Fujimura–Sugihara use velocity preprocessing based on neighboring frames. Missing intervals affected one otherwise position-observed frame immediately before and one immediately after the interval in the tested implementation. Position presence and derivative support are therefore separate validity dimensions.
--- ## Observation states uncovered by the investigation | Observation state | Current public behavior | Interpretation | |---|---|---| | Fully observed | Current percentages | Complete-data model estimate | | Partial Home dropout | Conserved conditional repartition | Conditional on observed Home players | | Partial Away dropout | Conserved conditional repartition | Conditional on observed Away players | | Partial bilateral dropout | Conserved conditional repartition | Conditional on both observed subsets | | Home entirely unobserved | `0/100` | Away-only partition | | Away entirely unobserved | `100/0` | Home-only partition | | Both teams entirely unobserved | `0/0` | No estimable ownership observation | | Motion-neighbor affected | Finite percentages | Positions present, derivative support affected | The proposed initial repair addresses only the categorically unambiguous aggregation defect: ```text both teams fully unobserved → no assigned owner exists → return NaN ``` The other states require broader policy or API design. --- ## Recommended initial repair: no-owner `NaN` guard A disposable local prototype used one private shared predicate derived directly from the existing ownership grid: ```python def _frames_have_assigned_owners(self) -> np.ndarray: return np.any(np.isfinite(self._cell_controls_), axis=(1, 2)) ``` Both `player_controls()` and `team_controls()` use the same predicate after their existing percentage calculations. The predicate name intentionally states only that an owner exists. It does not claim that the frame is fully observed, scientifically complete, or valid for every analytical purpose. ### Proposed semantics | Internal ownership state | Proposed public behavior | |---|---| | At least one assigned owner | Preserve all current percentages exactly | | No assigned owner | Every retained player and both teams become `NaN` | | Frame indexing and count | Preserved | | Denominator and rounding | Unchanged | | Ownership producer | Unchanged | | Motion preprocessing | Unchanged | | Grid construction | Unchanged | | Public signatures and return types | Unchanged | --- ## Local prototype feasibility evidence The disposable prototype modified only `floodlight/models/space.py`. Production diff: ```text 12 additions 0 removals 1 new private symbol 0 new public symbols ``` Results: - 174/174 assigned-frame outputs were exactly identical - 0 assigned frames changed - all 18 fully missing model/mesh results changed from zero to `NaN` - all fully missing frames remained retained and aligned - all 90 one-team and partial-dropout comparisons remained exactly unchanged - all 18 empty-team boundary combinations gained no new exception or shape regression - focused tests: 66/66 passed - existing space-control tests: 18/18 passed - all model tests: 134/134 passed - downstream temporal/zone tests: 28/28 passed - complete repository suite: 345/345 passed - Black, Flake8, and `git diff --check` passed A controlled mutation replaced the four `NaN` assignments with `0.0`. All 12 selected missing-output regression tests failed on the intended assertions. Restoring `NaN` caused all 12 to pass again. The prototype was not committed, pushed, or proposed for merge. --- ## Solution directions considered These directions address different contracts. They are not equivalent implementations of the same repair. | Direction | Problem addressed | Additional state or API | Maintenance surface | Proposed status | |---|---|---|---|---| | No-owner `NaN` guard | Fully undefined ownership becomes numeric zero | Existing ownership grid only | Low | Recommended initial PR | | One-team observation guard | Missing opposition becomes `100/0` | Retained input-observation state | Medium | Separate policy discussion | | Observation-quality sidecar | Missingness is not publicly communicated | New metadata/public lifecycle | High initially | Separate RFC/design issue | | Finite-owner denominator | Attempts to exclude undefined cells | Formula change | Adds little value | Rejected | | Motion-support validity | Derivatives depend on missing neighboring frames | Velocity-stencil support state | Separate contract | Follow-up design | ### Recommended: no-owner `NaN` guard Advantages: - repairs the only categorically undefined public output; - uses the missing state already preserved internally; - requires no new public interface or retained input state; - leaves every assigned frame unchanged; - applies consistently to all models and meshes; - has a small, testable, shared implementation boundary. Limitations are deliberate: one-team dropout remains `100/0`, partial-player dropout remains conditional, and motion derivative support remains undisclosed. ### Broader policy alternative: one-team observation guard A stronger policy could require at least one observed player from each team. Potentially, if either team is entirely unobserved, all player and team outputs for that frame would become `NaN`. Scientific advantage: - prevents missing-opposition `100/0` from appearing as a complete tactical estimate. Maintenance and compatibility cost: - percentages alone cannot distinguish legitimate complete `100/0` from missing-team `100/0`; - input-observation state must be retained or propagated from `fit()`; - deliberately one-sided inputs and tracking dropout need distinct semantics; - existing one-team behavior changes; - broader player/team consistency rules are required. The experiment strongly motivates this discussion, but the policy belongs to maintainers and should not be combined silently with the narrow repair. ### Longer-term API alternative: observation-quality sidecar Potential information could include: ```text position_observation_status observed_home_players observed_away_players home_observed_fraction away_observed_fraction both_teams_observed motion_support_valid ``` Advantages: - communicates incomplete observation without automatically discarding every conditional estimate; - distinguishes per-team observation completeness; - can separately disclose position presence and derivative support. Design and maintenance cost: - requires a new public contract; - may affect slicing, copying, resampling, pandas conversion, serialization, plotting, and downstream consumers; - counts and fractions are identity-blind and insufficient as validity criteria; - overall coverage hides team asymmetry; - owned-cell fraction is degenerate; - one flat enum may be insufficient. At least three independent dimensions may coexist: ```text position-observation completeness temporal missingness pattern motion-derivative support ``` This is better treated as a separate RFC or design issue. ### Rejected: finite-owned-cell denominator Replacing `owned count / all cells` with `owned count / finite owner cells` was rejected because the current producer normally assigns every grid cell whenever any valid player remains. Consequently, it does not detect one-team or partial-player dropout, still returns a conserved conditional 100% partition, changes the aggregation formula, and produces missingness for the fully undefined case only indirectly through a zero denominator. The explicit no-owner guard communicates the intended semantics more clearly and with less technical debt. ### Separate contract: motion-support validity Position observation and derivative support are not the same state. Taki–Hasegawa and Fujimura–Sugihara may depend on missing coordinates in neighboring frames even when the current frame's positions are finite. A future motion-support field requires a precise definition of derivative-stencil support, potentially at player rather than frame level. This should not be solved by changing or interpolating velocities in this proposal. ---
Adjacent findings intentionally excluded from the initial repair The investigation also reproduced or identified adjacent technical contracts: - half-missing coordinate pairs can bypass the full-frame skip and raise an all-`NaN` reduction error; - empty teams can produce a malformed empty player-property shape `(0,)`; - exact ownership ties favor the first stacked player identifier; - input validation is permissive for sequence lengths, framerates, coordinate pairs, and empty teams; - motion-model missingness can affect neighboring valid frames. These findings are not required to repair fully no-owner aggregation semantics and should not be combined into the initial PR without explicit maintainer agreement.
--- ## Historical context The all-cell aggregation behavior was introduced before Floodlight began preserving all-`NaN` ownership frames. A later change taught the ownership producer to skip completely missing frames and retain their internal `NaN` state, but the public player/team aggregators were not updated to preserve that missingness. The current `0/0` behavior therefore appears likely incidental rather than an explicitly documented missing-output policy. --- ## Why the proposed initial scope remains narrow The broader findings do not weaken the no-owner repair. They explain why it should not silently define unrelated policy. The proposed initial PR would address only: ```text no assigned owner exists → expose NaN for every player and both teams ``` It would not decide one-team-only policy, partial-player semantics, observation metadata, motion derivative support, or malformed-input validation. Those questions have materially different state, API, and maintenance requirements and should become separate follow-up issues or an RFC after maintainer feedback. --- ## Explicit exclusions The proposed initial repair would not: - change one-team or partial-dropout behavior; - change motion or velocity preprocessing; - add observation-quality metadata; - add or change public method signatures; - change `PlayerProperty` or `TeamProperty`; - validate half-missing coordinate pairs; - repair empty-team output shapes; - change exact-tie behavior; - change percentage denominators or rounding; - change mesh generation or model equations; - interpolate missing positions; - omit frames. --- ## Proposed acceptance criteria - no-owner frames remain temporally aligned; - every retained player and both teams are `NaN` on no-owner frames; - every assigned-frame player and team output remains exactly unchanged; - player and team aggregation share one private no-owner rule; - all three models and both mesh types are covered; - valid/missing/valid sequences preserve order and adjacent valid output; - one-team and partial-dropout behavior is not changed; - empty-team behavior is not worsened; - output classes, normal shapes, names, and framerate remain unchanged; - no public API, denominator, rounding, producer, motion, grid, or tie-policy change is introduced; - focused tests and the complete suite pass; - lint and `git diff --check` pass; - regression tests fail if `NaN` is replaced with zero. --- ## Maintainer questions 1. Should a frame with no assigned owner expose `NaN` for every player and both team-control outputs instead of numeric zero? 2. Is the aggregation-only no-owner guard an acceptable scope for an initial PR? 3. Should one-team observation policy and observation-quality metadata remain separate follow-up discussions? 4. Is a changelog entry expected for this numerical missingness correction? 5. Are there known downstream compatibility expectations for fully unobserved space-control frames that the eventual PR should preserve?

title: fix: fixed calculation of differences
body:
This fixes the unwanted behavior of the numpy gradient and diff functions to replace the first/last value of a NaN-free sequence with a NaNs. The differentiated data now has values where the original data has values and vice versa. This is achieved by the same approach we used to get the filterable sequences for the low pass filter.
Additionally, a minor bug in the call of the numpy diff function was fixed.

fix: compare SkillCorner ball IDs by value
body:
## Summary

The SkillCorner parser currently associates ball observations using Python object identity:

```python
pID is ball_id
```

Match metadata and positional tracking data are decoded from separate JSON files. Equal provider identifiers are therefore not guaranteed to refer to the same Python object, even though they represent the same ball.

This can silently leave valid ball coordinates as `NaN`.

## Change

Use identifier value equality for ball association:

```python
pID == ball_id
```

The production change is limited to this predicate.

## Regression protection

Added a compact synthetic regression test that:

* Writes match metadata and positional observations to independent JSON files.
* Calls the public `read_position_data_json` parser.
* Uses value-equal ball identifiers decoded independently.
* Verifies the exact expected ball coordinates.
* Verifies Home and Away player coordinates remain correct.
* Verifies the ball output shape and framerate.

No proprietary provider data are included.

## Measured result

On the deterministic regression fixture:

| Metric                                 |       Before |           After |
| -------------------------------------- | -----------: | --------------: |
| Correctly associated ball observations |          0/1 |             1/1 |
| Ball-association recall                |           0% |            100% |
| Returned ball coordinate               | `[NaN, NaN]` | `[12.5, -3.25]` |
| Valid ball rows left `NaN`             |            1 |               0 |
| Coordinate error                       |            — |    `[0.0, 0.0]` |

Home and Away control outputs remain unchanged.

## Validation

* Focused SkillCorner regression: `1 passed`
* SkillCorner test module: `1 passed`
* IO test suite: `9 passed`
* Full test suite: `280 passed`
* CI-equivalent full suite with coverage: `280 passed`
* Pre-commit: passed
* Black: passed
* Changed-file flake8: passed with zero findings
* Import smoke: passed
* Package build: passed

The full-repository flake8 output retains exactly two pre-existing unrelated `E226` findings. This change introduces no new lint findings.

## Scope

This PR does not change:

* SkillCorner schema support
* Coordinate handling
* Framerate
* Possession handling
* Filtering or interpolation
* Ball smoothing
* Other provider integrations
* Public API structure
* Dependencies

title: [FEAT] Kloppy integration to `floodlight.io`
body:
**Checklist**
- [X] I believe the feature fits the scope of the project

**Is your feature request related to a problem? Please describe.**
As discussed on the Building Bridges calls I think it would be good to have a starting place to start a discussion on allowing kloppy as a way to parse data, to integrate with floodlight.

**Describe the solution you'd like**
Given the structure of the project I'm not a 100% sure how to do this, but I can imagine we add a `floodlight.io.kloppy` that imports kloppy (throw error if not installed, no need to have it be a dependency) and then leverage kloppy to return all information you'd need to create the `data_objects` as shown in [`floodlight.io.secondspectrum`](https://github.com/floodlight-sports/floodlight/blob/main/floodlight/io/secondspectrum.py). 

For this to work we'd need to know the exact requirements that floodlight expects. E.g. coordinate systems, periods, timestamps, how are the teamsheets structured, are the xy_objects per period etc.

I'm just putting this here to get the conversation going on this!
